reason: The elite figures in this passage—Moses, Joshua, Aaron, and Hur—are all portrayed extremely favorably. Moses is depicted as a wise strategist and conduit of divine power whose actions directly determine the battle's outcome; Joshua is obedient and victorious; Aaron and Hur are loyal supporters. Only Amalek, a foreign adversary rather than part of the Israelite elite, is portrayed unfavorably as the defeated enemy. The narrative celebrates the leadership and faithfulness of Israel's elite figures.
